chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Abu Zayd al-Hallal, from Abdul Hameed ibn Abu al-A'la al-Azdi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed five (obligations) upon His creatures, so He granted concession in four, and did not grant concession in one.
ai.seo_question: What are the five pillars imposed by Allah and which one allows no concession?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the five foundational pillars of Islam, emphasizing that while Allah granted concessions (rukhsah) in four of them, one pillar remains absolute with no flexibility. In Shia scholarly tradition, this non-negotiable pillar is identified as Wilayah (divine guardianship), underscoring its essential role alongside prayer, fasting, zakat, and hajj. The distinction reflects the theological view that Wilayah is the spiritual core that validates the other acts of worship.
